aggressive_definition_excerpt: intake of tomato sauce, the primary source of bioavailable lycopene, was associated with an even greater reduction in prostate cancer risk (RR for 2+ servings/week versus <1 serving/month = 0.77; 95% CI = 0.66 to 0.90; P(trend)<.001), especially for extraprostatic cancers (RR = 0.65; 95% CI = 0.42 to 0.99).
study_design: Prospective cohort study (Health Professionals Follow-Up Study).
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We ascertained prostate cancer cases from 1986 through January 31, 1998, among 47 365 HPFS participants who completed dietary questionnaires in 1986, 1990, and 1994.
reason: The prospective cohort abstract reports total incident prostate cancer and separately reports an association for extraprostatic cancers, an aggressive incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: lycopene intake was associated with reduced risk of prostate cancer (RR for high versus low quintiles = 0.84; 95% CI = 0.73 to 0.96; P(trend) =.003)
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate is for overall incident prostate cancer, not the separately mentioned extraprostatic endpoint.
